questions.answer: Energy cannot be created or destroyed; it is transferred from one store to another. Input energy that is not transferred usefully is transferred to other stores or surroundings, so it is not missing.
accepted_alternatives: Total energy remains constant, with non-useful output transferred to other stores such as thermal energy or sound.

marking_points.text: States that energy cannot be created or destroyed, or that total energy is conserved.
Explains that energy not transferred usefully is transferred to other stores or the surroundings rather than disappearing.

questions.answer: B: useful energy output / total energy input

option_feedback.A: This reverses the ratio and can produce a value greater than 1.
option_feedback.B: Correct. Efficiency compares the useful output with the total input.
option_feedback.C: This compares two outputs and does not measure the useful fraction of the input.
option_feedback.D: Efficiency is a ratio, not a sum.

marking_points.text: Selects option B: useful energy output divided by total energy input.

questions.answer: C: 75% of the input energy is transferred usefully.
questions.unit_policy: Percentage symbol required when the answer is expressed as 75%.

option_feedback.A: A decimal efficiency of 0.75 corresponds to 75%, not 0.75%.
option_feedback.B: 25% is the non-useful fraction, not the useful fraction.
option_feedback.D: An efficiency of 0.75 means useful output is smaller than input.

marking_points.text: Selects option C: 75% of the input energy is transferred usefully.

option_feedback.A: This is the non-useful fraction, found from 1.50 - 0.960 and then divided by 1.50.
option_feedback.C: This reverses input and useful output.
option_feedback.D: 64 is the percentage number without its percent symbol, not a decimal efficiency.

marking_points.text: Selects option B: 0.64 from 0.960 kJ divided by 1.50 kJ.

parts.label: (a)
parts.unit_policy: Final response must be a percentage because percentage efficiency is requested.

marking_points.text: Forms the efficiency ratio as 3.15 kJ divided by 4.50 kJ and multiplies by 100%.
Obtains a percentage efficiency of 70.0%, or 70%.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: Non-useful energy = 4.50 - 3.15 = 1.35 kJ. Check: 3.15 kJ + 1.35 kJ = 4.50 kJ.
accepted_alternatives: 1350 J with the equivalent check 3150 J + 1350 J = 4500 J
parts.unit_policy: Accept kJ or consistently converted J.

marking_points.text: Calculates the non-useful transfer as 4.50 kJ minus 3.15 kJ = 1.35 kJ.
Checks that useful 3.15 kJ plus non-useful 1.35 kJ equals the 4.50 kJ input.
Uses charger P useful power output divided by its total power input: 22.0 W / 40.0 W.
Obtains charger P percentage efficiency as 55.0%, or 55%.
Uses charger Q useful power output divided by its total power input: 18.0 W / 30.0 W.
Obtains charger Q percentage efficiency as 60.0%, or 60%.

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: Charger Q is more efficient because 60% is greater than 55%. Useful output alone is insufficient because efficiency compares useful output with each charger's total input.
accepted_alternatives: Q is more efficient; P has the larger useful output but also the larger input, so the output-to-input ratios must be compared.

marking_points.text: Identifies charger Q as more efficient and explains that useful output must be compared with the corresponding total input rather than compared alone.
